note: PASS WITH CAVEATS. (1) CODE DERIVATION: exempt, pattern 1. data/mascherini_2021_meddiet.py melts the S1 File XLSX's own header row and lowercases it with spaces to underscores (ITEM_COLS = ['Grains','Potatoes','Fruits','Vegetables','Legumes','Fish','Red meat','White meat','Dairy ','Oil','Alchool'], then str.strip().str.lower().str.replace(' ','_')), so the IRW code IS the source column name -- 'Red meat' -> red_meat, 'Alchool' -> alchool (the source's own spelling of alcohol). All 11 headers reconcile 11/11 with the live item set. The headers name food groups, not questions, so they pin the MAPPING while the WORDS come from the S2 File questionnaire, matched food group to food group; that is the bitew_2020_osss3 shape. (2) LANGUAGE / TEXT SOURCE: fallback. The sample is 1383 University of Florence faculty, staff and students resident in Italy and the paper cites the Italian GPAQ (GPAQ_Italian.pdf), so the administration was Italian; the paper never states this in so many words, so language=Italian is an inference and is flagged as such here. The administered Italian is in neither supplement -- S2 File is the authors' own English rendering of the whole ABITUD-19 questionnaire and S1 File is numeric with English headers -- so the English ships in the base fields, the _translated columns are empty, text_source=translated_substitute and translation_source=study_supplied. (3) WAVE / TENSE: the live table pools both waves under one item code, and the S2 File prints each item twice, once past tense for 'BEFORE quarantine' (wave 1) and once present tense for 'DURING quarantine' (wave 2), identical apart from that tense ('How often did you eat potatoes in a week?' vs 'How often do you eat potatoes in a week?'). The past-tense wave-1 form ships; see public_note. (4) RESP AXIS -- the inference that was actually checked. The questionnaire prints six frequency bands per food group in ascending order of consumption; resp 0-5 is the MedDietScore, which scores the eight foods close to the Mediterranean pattern 0..5 ascending and reverses red meat, white meat, full-fat dairy and alcohol. So option_text is mapped 0..5 in printed order for grains/potatoes/fruits/vegetables/legumes/fish/oil and 5..0 for red_meat/white_meat/dairy/alchool. Confirmed against the data, not assumed: the per-respondent sum of the 11 stored items equals the XLSX's own 'Mediterranean SCORE D' column for 1383/1383 rows in each wave, its wave-1 mean/SD is 30.99/4.15 against the paper's published 31.0/4.1, and flipping those four items would give 18.88 -- 12.1 points off. See verify_mascherini_2021_meddiet.R (VERDICT: PASS) and the verification sidecar. (5) TRANSCRIPTION, verbatim including source oddities: the red meat top band is printed '<8' where the ascending series requires '>8', the dairy series starts at '<10' with no 'Never' band, and 'How many times a week did you use cooking olive oil in a week?' repeats 'in a week'. All are shipped as printed, unfixed. Option tokens are the comma-separated fields of the questionnaire's own option line, whitespace-trimmed ('13-18,> 18' -> '> 18'); no other normalisation. (6) INSTRUCTIONS: the questionnaire's own participant-facing framing paragraph, verbatim. section_prompt is blank and section_id is the single trivial mascherini_2021_meddiet_1 -- the instrument has no testlet grouping. correct_response is blank: a food-frequency scale has no key. (7) STEP 3b: clean. The dictionary Description says Med Diet Score, 11 food groups, 0-5; the live item set is exactly the 11 MedDietScore food groups and the paper's Table 2 reproduces all 11 per-item means to <=0.049. The same paper's GPAQ and PGWBI-A blocks are not in this table (the processing script excludes them as composites). (8) RIGHTS: not blocked, and nothing quotable was found. The wording shipped is the study's own ABITUD-19 questionnaire, published by its authors as a CC BY 4.0 PLOS supplement. Checked upstream per the 2026-09-08 originator rule: the MedDietScore's rights holder (Panagiotakos et al., Harokopio University) publishes no terms page for the instrument that could be located, and no fee, permission-required, non-commercial, no-derivatives or no-redistribution clause could be found or quoted for it; under 'silence is permission' the rule does not fire. Note also that the ABITUD-19 items are an adaptation (weekly rather than monthly frequency bands), so what ships is the adapting authors' own wording. No row was added to itemtext/instrument_rights_register.csv because the register is a shared file and five sibling agents were writing in this batch; the MedDietScore is worth a 'ship' row and the orchestrator should add one. (9) AUDIT: no WARN expected -- every item carries all six of its own resp levels (66 rows = 11 x 6) and no option_text is padded with its resp value.
public_note: Each of the 11 food-frequency items was administered twice, once for habits before the COVID-19 lockdown (wave 1) and once for habits during it (wave 2); the two administrations differ only in tense, and the past-tense wave-1 wording is what ships. The study was run in Italian but publishes only the authors' own English version of the questionnaire, so item_text and option_text are that English rather than what respondents read. resp is the MedDietScore, not the raw frequency: for red meat, white meat, dairy products and alcohol a HIGH resp means LOW consumption, and the option_text on those four items is mapped accordingly.
